sources.title: W3C WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference
claims: Normative criteria cover reflow, focus appearance, target size, contrast, and animation from interactions.
Trend adoption cannot weaken perceivable, operable, understandable, or robust behavior.

sources.title: Material 3 Expressive: Engaging UX Design
claims: Current design-system guidance treats color, shape, hierarchy, and motion as coordinated expressive tools.
Expression must remain usable rather than becoming decoration without task value.

sources.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines
claims: Current platform guidance is a reference for hierarchy, consistency, legibility, and interaction clarity.
Distinctive branding should not displace familiar navigation and control behavior.

sources.title: Awwwards Sites of the Day, July 2026
claims: The July 1-4 feed includes Wembi, Units, Bucks Sauce, and Radian as current visual exemplars.
The feed is inspiration evidence, not a normative usability authority.

assessments.observation: The hero and chrome establish a clear primary brand signal, but the relationship between brand, navigation, and secondary actions can be made more deliberate.
assessments.recommendation: Preserve the strong wordmark while tightening spacing, action priority, and cross-page hierarchy tokens.

assessments.observation: The red-ring wordmark is distinctive and memorable, but the same visual signature is not yet expressed as a broader component language.
assessments.recommendation: Extend the ring, typography, and warm coffee palette into a small reusable brand-token family instead of adding unrelated decoration.

assessments.observation: The reviewed widths are controlled, but the narrow breakpoint behavior required corrective overrides and should be treated as a first-class layout contract.
assessments.recommendation: Promote 320-340px composition, text reflow, and chrome collision checks into permanent visual evidence.

assessments.observation: Accessible text remains in the DOM and browser gates are strong, but future visual experiments must preserve focus, contrast, target size, and reduced-motion behavior.
assessments.recommendation: Make WCAG-backed constraints hard guards for every visual trend experiment.

assessments.observation: Motion is restrained and safe, but it does not yet reinforce the coffee journey, product transitions, or spatial hierarchy.
assessments.recommendation: Test one small expressive transition at a time with reduced-motion and performance guards.

assessments.observation: The site has a strong hero and useful discovery surface, but the visual journey between coffee, food, place, and social context is still fragmented.
assessments.recommendation: Build a coherent editorial sequence using product close-ups, human moments, and one clear visit narrative rather than a collection of isolated sections.

patternDecisions.label: Extend the distinctive wordmark into reusable brand tokens
patternDecisions.rationale: The existing mark is already recognizable; systematizing it improves consistency without chasing a temporary style.
riskNotes: Avoid repeating the ring motif so often that it becomes visual noise.

patternDecisions.label: Expressive micro-motion for product and journey transitions
patternDecisions.rationale: Current exemplars use motion to create emotion, but Roby's should test motion only where it explains state or advances the story.
riskNotes: Motion may increase cognitive load or regress low-end mobile performance.
patternDecisions.experimentGuard: Require prefers-reduced-motion coverage, no layout shift, a bounded animation budget, and exact-head visual evidence.

patternDecisions.label: Tactile editorial texture and close-up product imagery
patternDecisions.rationale: A warmer, more tactile layer fits the coffee-house identity better than generic polished gradients.
riskNotes: Heavy imagery can reduce text contrast and increase page weight.
patternDecisions.experimentGuard: Keep text contrast at WCAG AA, preserve a fixed media budget, and compare conversion and scroll completion against the current surface.

patternDecisions.label: Experimental novelty navigation
patternDecisions.rationale: Award-site novelty is not sufficient reason to reduce predictable navigation for a local cafe customer journey.
riskNotes: Hidden or unconventional navigation can reduce discoverability and keyboard clarity.
